plates.name: 卢舍那大佛
plates.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit, color-in an existing drawing.
You are coloring an existing architectural atlas plate, NOT redrawing it. The attached black-on-white artwork is the EXACT geometry master. Treat its contour and all internal structural lines as locked. Only replace the white regions INSIDE the existing object with mineral color fills, and replace the white outside the object with a perfectly flat near-black background.
The desired style is a restrained Chinese mineral-gouache hand-colored engraving: fine delicate contour lines with thin semi-flat muted color areas, a little dry-pigment granulation, and at most two gentle shadow tones. Stay GRAPHIC and illustration-like, keep broad areas calm. The finished subject has color and substance, but the elegance and airy detail of the original line drawing remain dominant.
Keep original canvas size/aspect ratio and EXACT same object position, scale, silhouette, roof profile, openings, ornament, and perspective. No zooming or reframing, no changes to anatomy/architecture. Do not invent new surfaces or ornament. No filled paper rectangle, no frame, typography, watermark, plaque lettering, sky, people, plants, scene, lights or ground shadow.
Backdrop must be perfectly uniform solid near-black RGB(16,15,13), hex #100f0d, all the way to all four edges. This is a dark-background concept sample for the website. Do NOT draw checkerboards, transparency grids, white backgrounds, halos, atmospheric gradients, paper outside the object, or vignette. Interior open doorways and spaces between columns remain the same dark backdrop.
Use thin dynasty-colored or slightly darker brown contour strokes, never thick black cartoon outlines. Clear but restrained material coloring, not a photograph, metallic gold sculpture, shiny 3D model, or thick oil paint. Output one standalone plate without UI or before/after panels.

SUBJECT: Longmen Vairocana Buddha BUST exactly as input. Preserve its broken forearms, irregular foreground stone shapes, and exact facial drawing. This reference is not a full standing or seated figure: never extend it. The tip of the hair bun must stay at about y=165 on the 1024x1536 canvas; the face, ears, shoulders and broken stones must align to the supplied contours, including the loose open lower endpoints. Do not enlarge the head or give the face a different expression. Thin incomplete lower contours can fade into the dark; do not invent a new jagged horizontal cutoff or an additional pedestal.
COLOR: Tang warm gold #d6ab5c remains the delicate outline accent. Fill face, neck and robe with muted sandstone #bba17a and warm ivory #d2bf99; restrained umber #75654e shadows in the existing folds; hair in subdued stone grey-brown. Keep everything recognizably stone, including the robe, with no colored clothing costume. Some open reserves around folds and along the bottom should remain dark and airy. Pigment is much thinner and less mottled than an aged stone texture study. Final visual should feel gently illuminated from within its colored planes, not glossy or gilded. PORTRAIT 1024 x 1536.
